outcome: Offspring complications (low birth weight, low Apgar Score, need of CPAP or NICU, congenital malformations, incidence of osteogenesis imperfecta, birth related fractures, hospital contacts during the first year of life)
cohort: The study included all pregnancies registered in Danish health registers from 1997 to 2018 where one parent had Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI), and a reference population of all other pregnancies.
finding: Pregnancies with parental Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI) showed similar rates of pregnancy and delivery complications compared to a reference population, resulting in live births to term with very few complications.
mod_finding: A higher percentage of children in the Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI) cohort (31%) were delivered by caesarean section compared to the reference population (19%).
